asks: Keep Edmonton-North West's current boundaries; do not push it west into Big Lake-area neighbourhoods or south of the Yellowhead.
Move the southern cut line (to Highway 623 or 616) so her corner of Leduc County returns to Leduc-Beaumont, and do not put Beaumont in an Edmonton riding.
Keep municipalities intact (Calgary-Varsity resident describing her urban community).
Keep like communities together (urban and rural apart) and give the two new seats to Edmonton and Calgary.
Avoid mixing large urban and rural communities in ridings and keep population differences minimal.
Keep the Weaselhead, Glenmore Reservoir and surrounding communities within Calgary-Glenmore.
Keep Edmonton-North West intact, north of the Yellowhead and west of 97 Street, without adding neighbourhoods.
Stop weighting rural votes over urban votes.
Leave Edmonton-Rutherford as is, or if redrawn keep its neighbourhoods grouped with other mature urban neighbourhoods.
Redraw the western boundary of Bonnyville-Cold Lake-St. Paul to follow the MD of Bonnyville and County of St. Paul lines, moving Saddle Lake Cree Nation to Athabasca-Barrhead-Westlock.
Do not combine rural and urban populations in one riding; add the two new ridings in a way that keeps communities whole.
Create four Lethbridge-anchored electoral divisions (Lethbridge-Cardston, -Livingstone, -Little Bow, -Taber) joining the city with surrounding towns such as Coaldale.

quote: That’s why I am writing to support the proposal to create four new electoral divisions (depicted in Annex A below) that more accurately reflect how southern Alberta is organized and connected.
note: Deputy Mayor of Coaldale, round 1. Names the four: Lethbridge-Cardston, Lethbridge-Livingstone, Lethbridge-Little Bow, Lethbridge-Taber; Annex B (p. 5) divides the city's population among the four. Also criticises Cardston-Siksika as too large.

asks: Keep urban Calgary ridings (Calgary-Foothills area) within municipal boundaries, do not mix rural areas with large urban centres, and give new seats to Calgary and Edmonton.
Leave Livingstone-Macleod intact as it is, neither enlarged nor split.

note: Lethbridge named only as one place her Nanton customers come from; no request about it.

asks: Limit population variation to about 5%, leave room for growth, and keep Calgary-Acadia's natural boundaries (Bow River, Fish Creek Park, Glenmore Trail).
Make the City of Medicine Hat its own electoral division, separate from Brooks.
Keep Calgary-Foothills within the City of Calgary boundaries, with no rural area added.
Make Medicine Hat its own distinct urban riding, not divided and not grouped with Brooks or rural areas.
Keep Calgary-Shaw's boundaries as they are, including the southern boundary at the city limit.
Give Medicine Hat its own riding instead of splitting the city and joining it to rural districts.
Keep the Symons Valley suburban communities of north Calgary (Sage Hill, Nolan Hill, Kincora, Sherwood, Evanston) represented together as suburban communities, apart from rural neighbours.

note: Red Deer named only as where the writer and his wife grew up; no request about it.

asks: Redraw Banff-Kananaskis as a mountain 'Banff-Jasper-Kananaskis' riding reaching east only to Highway 22; put the two new seats in Calgary and Edmonton; hold districts within 15% of average; follow municipal boundaries; consider First Nations ridings.

quote: provincial election district boundaries should follow municipal boundaries. For example, might Airdrie now qualify as an electoral riding.
note: Put as a question, offered as an example of following municipal boundaries; reads as a suggestion of an Airdrie-only riding. Canmore resident; his main request concerns Banff-Kananaskis and Jasper (context element, not coded here).

asks: Preserve the existing boundaries of Calgary-Hays.
Add a seat in each of Calgary and Edmonton and keep constituencies in Edmonton, Calgary and other growing cities such as Lethbridge wholly inside municipal borders.

quote: democratic fairness is best served by ensuring that electoral constituencies in Edmonton, Calgary, and other expanding municipalities, such as but not limited to Lethbridge, are housed exclusively inside municipal borders.
note: Asks for city-only constituencies and names Lethbridge as one such city; does not say how many. Goes on to call urban-rural combinations 'unlike for unlike' in general terms, not about Lethbridge specifically.

asks: Replace Cardston-Siksika, Livingstone-Macleod, Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West with four Lethbridge-anchored divisions (Lethbridge-Cardston, -Livingstone, -Little Bow, -Taber).

quote: we support the proposed elimination of the current electoral divisions of Cardston-Siksika, Livingstone-Macleod, Lethbridge-East, and Lethbridge-West in favour of four new, more cohesive and representative divisions depicted in Annex A below
note: Coaldale Chamber of Commerce, round 1. Same four-division proposal and annexes as EBC-2025-1-0101 (different wording, so not a word-for-word campaign copy). Supports eliminating Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West but does not argue against city-only ridings as such, so no rejects.

asks: Prioritize municipal boundaries so Calgary-Lougheed communities are not grouped with areas outside Calgary.
Make Medicine Hat an urban-only riding, not grouped with Brooks or rural areas.
Keep Calgary-Foothills and other urban ridings urban, and add ridings in the northern suburbs of Calgary and in Edmonton.
If Edmonton-Rutherford must change, extend it north across Whitemud Drive rather than keep Twin Brooks; attend to the oversized Edmonton-South and Edmonton-Ellerslie.
Keep Lethbridge West and Lethbridge East within the municipal boundary, keep small towns such as Coalhurst out of city ridings, and add seats in fast-growing urban areas.

quote: I would not want to see boundary lines drawn that meant the municipal boundary was not maintained for Lethbridge West and Lethbridge East. For over 100 years the ridings of Lethbridge have been bound by the municipal boundary and I believe that is the way that it should remain.
note: Coalhurst resident who works in Lethbridge West. Rejects any joining of city and surrounding towns (so both the four-way plan and lesser hybrids), round 1, before any proposal; also p. 46: 'If our provincial boundaries meant that my small town would be lumped into a riding with Lethbridge residents their sheer population would dominate ours'.

Airdrie named only as an example of places with very large ridings ('Some ridings in Edmonton, Airdrie, and Calgary are huge'); asks for more urban seats in general, nothing about how Airdrie is divided.

asks: Keep Calgary-Glenmore's Jewish community together in the constituency and give Calgary an additional seat.
Keep Lethbridge's electoral districts within the city's municipal boundary; do not extend them into rural areas.

quote: Expanding electoral boundaries beyond the municipality of Lethbridge risks diluting the representation of urban residents, particularly newcomer and ethnocultural communities.
note: Lethbridge resident, round 1. The request itself follows on p. 53: 'I respectfully urge the Commission to maintain the integrity of Lethbridge’s municipal boundary in its electoral map.' Argues against any extension of Lethbridge ridings beyond the city, so both the four-way plan and lesser hybrids are rejected; no proposal existed yet.

asks: Keep Highwood's boundaries the same or very similar.
Leave Edmonton-North West's boundaries alone.
Keep Edmonton-North West largely as it is now.

Keep St. Albert and Morinville-St. Albert basically unchanged (at most trade Redwater for St. Albert growth areas), never join Edmonton or Calgary to surrounding ridings, pair like with like, and use the one-urban-seat-plus-one-mixed-seat model for other small cities.

quote: any move to change or split the boundaries of the stand-alone St. Albert riding to bulk up underpopulated rural ridings – for example, Lac-Ste. Anne-Parkland – would also be extremely poorly received by residents
note: Want shown on p. 64: 'this Commission should follow the example set by past Commissions and maintain a wholly-urban St. Albert riding paired with a north-reaching riding that include St. Albert, Morinville, and other culturally and economically-linked Sturgeon County communities'; p. 67: 'Both St. Albert ridings are excellent and should remain largely unchanged.' The quoted rejection is of carving the St. Albert riding for Lac Ste. Anne-Parkland, which is the distinguishing feature of S2. Also rejects adding parts of Edmonton to St. Albert. Fallback adjustments if growth requires: extend Morinville-St. Albert west to Jensen Lakes, Elysian Fields, Deer Ridge and Northridge and drop Redwater to Athabasca-Barrhead-Westlock; or return the city's north-east corner to St. Albert (2012 lines). Does not ask for all of Sturgeon County in the hybrid, so not S1.

quote: they also provide an example that I would submit the Commission should follow when reviewing the boundaries of all of Alberta’s ‘small-urban’ constituencies, like Medicine Hat, Airdrie, Grande Prairie, etc. This combination of a wholly-urban seat with a mixed rural-urban seat
note: A9: one seat wholly inside Airdrie plus one mixed Airdrie-rural seat, on the St. Albert model; Airdrie is named in a list of cities, not discussed on its own. On p. 62 he expects Airdrie to warrant two wholly-urban ridings within two boundary cycles. His general rule (p. 67) that 'Edmonton and Calgary should not be integrated into surrounding small-urban or rural ridings in any capacity' cuts against A2 but does not name Airdrie in that sentence, so no rejects coded.
Lethbridge named as a comparison only: a city that already has two wholly-urban ridings (pp. 62, 64). Described approvingly but no request about it.
Red Deer named as a comparison only: a city that already has two wholly-urban ridings (pp. 62, 64). Described approvingly but no request about it.

asks: Leave the Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West boundaries as they are; the growth to deal with is in Edmonton and Calgary.

quote: I see no rationale or compelling need for the current electoral boundaries for Lethbridge East or Lethbridge West to be adjusted.
note: Lethbridge resident, round 1. Also p. 72: 'In the case of Lethbridge, those lines can remain the same.'

asks: Keep Lethbridge's two city constituencies and create the two new seats by redistribution in the Calgary, Edmonton and Airdrie area.

quote: Lethbridge is well served by the two current constituencies, Lethbridge West and Lethbridge East.
note: Statement of satisfaction with the two city ridings rather than a formal request, backed by 'The concerns of Lethbridge citizens are much different that the rural areas surrounding our city' and the ask that new seats go elsewhere. No words of rejection aimed at a hybrid plan.

Says the two new constituencies should come from 'a redistribution in the Calgary, Edmonton, Airdrie area'; a request for an added seat in that area, nothing about how the City of Airdrie is divided or whom it is joined with.

asks: Make no redistribution that affects Fort McKay First Nation: keep it whole within Fort McMurray-Wood Buffalo and consult First Nations before any change.
Do not combine Calgary neighbourhoods with rural or town communities outside the city in one electoral division.
Maintain Edmonton-Castle Downs's existing boundaries and do not add neighbouring rural communities to it; seats should follow growth in south Edmonton and north Calgary.
Keep St. Albert whole and intact rather than split between a city riding and the urban-rural Morinville-St. Albert riding, and add seats for south Edmonton and north Calgary.

quote: any new electoral map keep our urban community intact. When residents feel fragmented between ridings — as parts of St. Albert do in the current Morinville-St. Albert (MVSA) configuration — they may begin to question whether their vote truly counts.
note: St. Albert resident, round 1. Asks that St. Albert be kept whole and criticises the current division of the city into the Morinville-St. Albert hybrid; also p. 85: 'Maintaining municipal boundaries within a single riding would allow representatives to more consistently and effectively address the issues'. She does not say how a city of this size would be seated, so S3 at direction. The objection to the hybrid reaches S1 and S2 as well, since both keep one; coded as S0 because she names only the current configuration.

asks: Add more than two seats, since Airdrie and nearby areas have grown over 20%, and draw the maps fairly.

note: Airdrie named as an example of fast growth that two added seats do not cover; nothing about how the city is divided or whom it is joined with.

asks: Keep the St. Albert part of Morinville-St. Albert together in that riding with Morinville, Legal and Bon Accord.

quote: The urban part of MVSA (St. Albert section) is growing quite quickly and should definitely stay together.
note: Resident of the St. Albert part of Morinville-St. Albert; speaks well of the half-urban, half-rural riding and wants its city section kept together in it. Ends: 'This new grouping (St. Albert east, Morinville, Legal and Bon-Accord) will be approximately the population size of an average sized (47,000) riding', which leaves out Gibbons and Redwater and may imply a trimmed hybrid; he does not say so outright.

asks: Do not add communities outside Calgary to Calgary ridings, and place one of the two new seats in Calgary.
Leave the two Lethbridge city districts unchanged; do not split them and join them to surrounding rural areas.

quote: the boundaries of the two electoral districts that represent the urban area of Lethbridge should remain unchanged. There have been public comments made that have spurred me to write to you related to splitting these urban electoral areas and including the surrounding rural areas. I am not in support
note: University of Lethbridge geography professor, round 1. Reacting to public talk of splitting the city ridings and joining them to the country (an idea on no map at the time); wants the current two city districts. The sentence continues: 'of altering the boundaries of urban electoral districts to include populations that are not part of the same community.'

asks: Draw constituencies around how people live, not municipal lines, so that places just outside Calgary such as Conrich are in a Calgary-based district.
Keep Lake Louise, Banff, Canmore and Exshaw together in one district with room for growth, and do not lump the Bow Valley mountain communities with agricultural areas such as around Sundre.

quote: It would be a disservice to both communities to be lumped together.
note: Canmore resident, round 1. Says 'the communities of Lake Louise, Banff, Canmore and Exshaw are intertwined and inseparable' and that the agricultural country near Sundre, where she once ran cattle, should not be lumped with the Bow Valley mountain communities. That is the substance of B2 (park and MD of Bighorn kept with Banff and Canmore, apart from the foothills riding), but she never names Rocky Mountain House, Clearwater County or the riding, so by the codebook's RMH-B caution and rule 17 no want is coded. A second reader may fairly code B2 at direction. Sundre is named only as the place of her former land; no request about which riding Sundre belongs in (no RMH-A or OLDS-A line).
